head: 5809f30c77db2e6e74ab8378ac98573e2f859aee
summary:
SL-005 works on every system I could reach. A folder deleted during a scan is counted as deleted, not as unreadable. When the path above a folder stops resolving, the folder still stays unreadable. Two builds were compared in fresh Windows Sandboxes, running as administrator (SYSTEM): the fix at HEAD 5809f30, and a second scan program built from the pre-slice code (uat 28d72d8). Both used the real Scanner.Scan.

**Deleting folders mid-scan, fix against pre-slice:** a root child is deleted after the root is listed, so its open fails with 2. A folder under a deleted parent fails with 3. I ran this on local NTFS, a ReFS volume, a loopback SMB share (\\127.0.0.1) and a drive letter mapped to that share:
- Pre-slice: both folders are recorded unreadable (Unreadable 2, codes 2 and 3, NothingListed).
- Fix: FoldersVanished 2, Unreadable 0, VanishedBeforeProbe 1. Each deleted subtree is counted once.

**Losing the path above the folder mid-scan:** the queued folders stay unreadable with FoldersVanished 0 in every case:
- Mapped letter removed (`net use /delete`): their opens fail with 3. The root check catches it.
- ReFS volume detached: same, opens fail with 3 and the root check catches it.
- Share removed: opens fail with 67, which is not a deleted-folder code.

**Live Sandbox C:\, 157,428 folders, with 5 root-level folders deleted 2 s in plus Windows' own activity:**
- The scan program at HEAD: Completed, FoldersVanished 8, Unreadable 0.
- The app published from HEAD, in report mode (`--report`): exit 0, core.foldersVanished 8, core.unreadable 0.
  - The note reads "8 folders were deleted while the scan ran, before they could be read; they are counted as empty folders."
  - The Unreadable tab is hidden, neither caption says 'missing', and the report has no non-ASCII characters.
  - The note is the 4th of 4 lines in a box 76 px tall with 160.96 px of content, so it may need scrolling. The build already filed this layout.

**Report exit codes:** a missing --report value gives 2, an unwritable report path gives 3, and a plain run gives 0 with foldersVanished 0 and no note.

**On this PC:** the whole suite passes (1346/1346) and Fitness says all 111 rules hold.

**Unrelated failure, also in the pre-slice build:** the scanner cannot open an exFAT or FAT32 root at all, even the volume root (RootUnreadable 87). So the FAT part of O-002 cannot be reached, and the app probably cannot scan exFAT or FAT USB sticks. That belongs on the backlog.

Not run: throw mode (exit 70), the window script on this PC's desktop, DFS, minifilters, a remote SMB server over a real network, and the person's own C:\, OneDrive and network proof runs.

The slice had one build attempt and one code review, so it is not looping. The bug report was only a title. The criteria I graded are the design's 14 cases.

checks.what: Whole suite at HEAD 5809f30
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx -- xUnit.MaxParallelThreads=2 (TAAD3_HOME = new empty temp folder)
checks.evidence: Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 1346, Skipped: 0, Total: 1346, Duration: 1 m 33 s; exit 0 in 97 s

checks.what: Architecture rules
checks.evidence: 111 rules checked against 214 parsed files: every declared rule holds (the proof-run rule matches no files, as docs/proof-runs is still empty)

checks.what: First publish attempt of the scan program and the app
checks.evidence: My command was malformed: PowerShell split -nodeReuse:false and MSBuild stopped with MSB1041. Nothing was built. Re-run below without the switch.

checks.what: Publish the scan program (real Scanner.Scan with ScanOptions.AfterFolder) and the app from HEAD, plus the same program against the pre-slice Core (git archive 28d72d853)
checks.command: eng/dotnet.ps1 publish %TEMP%\sl005-val-src\Probe.csproj -c Release -o .taad-scratch/sl005-val/probe; same for src/FsAnalyser.App -o .taad-scratch/sl005-val/app and probe-base
checks.evidence: probe exit 0, app exit 0, base probe exit 0; FsAnalyser.App.exe 139,997,336 B built 10:39:57

checks.what: Sandbox, local NTFS: z deleted while queued (open 2), y deleted after its own listing so y\w opens with 3; fix against pre-slice
checks.evidence: Raw opens: z -> 2, y\w -> 3. Fix: Completed folders=4 foldersVanished=2 vanishedBeforeProbe=1 unreadable=0. Pre-slice: unreadable=2 (z error 2 NothingListed, y\w error 3 NothingListed). Same result in both Sandbox runs.

checks.what: Sandbox, ReFS volume (50 GB vdisk, format /FS:ReFS): same deletions, fix against pre-slice
checks.command: Sandbox: probe R:\t with the same hooks, fix and base
checks.evidence: Raw opens: z -> 2, y\w -> 3. Fix: foldersVanished=2 unreadable=0. Pre-slice: unreadable=2 (codes 2 and 3).

checks.what: Sandbox, SMB loopback share \\127.0.0.1\sl5a, folders deleted on the server side mid-scan; fix against pre-slice
checks.evidence: Over SMB the opens return 2 (z) and 3 (y\w). Fix: Completed foldersVanished=2 unreadable=0. Pre-slice: unreadable=2 with codes 2 and 3.

checks.what: Sandbox, drive letter Y: mapped to the share, same deletions; fix against pre-slice
checks.command: Sandbox: net use Y: \\127.0.0.1\sl5d; probe Y:\t with hooks
checks.evidence: Opens: Y:\t\z -> 2, Y:\t\y\w -> 3. Fix: foldersVanished=2 unreadable=0. Pre-slice: unreadable=2.

checks.what: Sandbox, share removed mid-scan (net share sl5b /delete /y at folder 1)
checks.evidence: Opens after removal return 67 (ERROR_BAD_NET_NAME). Fix: Completed foldersVanished=0 unreadable=4, all 67 NothingListed, so they are not counted as deleted.

checks.what: Sandbox, mapped letter removed mid-scan (net use X: /delete /y at folder 1), the M1 case
checks.evidence: The queued folders' opens and the root's open both return 3. Fix: foldersVanished=0 unreadable=4 (3x4 NothingListed). The root check kept them unreadable.

checks.what: Sandbox, ReFS volume detached mid-scan (diskpart detach vdisk at folder 1, like pulling a USB disk)
checks.evidence: Detach succeeded. Opens of R:\u\b and R:\u return 3. Fix: foldersVanished=0 unreadable=4 (3x4). The root check kept them unreadable.

checks.what: Sandbox, exFAT (P:) and FAT32 (Q:) volumes, same deletion test
checks.command: Sandbox: probe P:\t, Q:\t, P:\, Q:\ with fix and base
checks.evidence: fsutil reports exFAT and FAT32, and dir P:\t shows a, y and z. But every scan ends RootUnreadable rootError=87 with no hook fired, even at the volume root, on BOTH the fix and the pre-slice program built from 28d72d853 in the same Sandbox run. The scanner cannot list exFAT or FAT32 roots at all, which is not caused by SL-005 (ListRoot is not in its diff), and it blocks the FAT part of O-002.

checks.what: Sandbox run 1: SMB loopback with networking off
checks.evidence: Every SMB access failed with 1231 (network location cannot be reached), because the Sandbox was started with networking off. Re-run with network on, above.

checks.what: Sandbox run 1: live C:\ scan program, 480 s limit
checks.command: Sandbox: probe C:\ with C:\zz-sl5-1..5 deleted at 2 s
checks.evidence: Killed at 480 s (first scan on a cold cache). My limit was too short and no output survived. Re-run in run 2 with 1,100 s.

checks.what: Sandbox live whole C:\ with the scan program at HEAD, 5 root folders deleted 2 s in, plus Windows' own deletions
checks.command: Sandbox run 2: Start-Process probe C:\; Remove-Item C:\zz-sl5-* at 2,053 ms
checks.evidence: RESULT status=Completed folders=157428 files=123560 foldersVanished=8 vanishedBeforeProbe=39 probeFailures=2 unreadable=0, 556 s. No unreadable rows of any code; the 3 deleted folders beyond my 5 came from Windows itself.

checks.what: Sandbox live whole C:\ with the app at HEAD in report mode, same timed deletion
checks.command: Sandbox run 1: FsAnalyser.App.exe C:\ --report C:\taad\out\app-c.json; Remove-Item C:\zz-sl5-* at 3,867 ms
checks.evidence: exit 0 in 390 s. Report fields: schema 1; core {status Completed, folders 157428, unreadable 0, foldersVanished 8}; OutcomeNotes line 4 is '8 folders were deleted while the scan ran, before they could be read; they are counted as empty folders.'; UnreadableTab visible false; LargestFilesCaption 'Top 100 of 123,169 files scanned.' and KindsCaption '123,169 files scanned, sorted by extension.', neither saying 'missing'; 0 non-ASCII characters. OutcomeTexts actualHeight 76 against extentHeight 160.96, so the note may need scrolling; this layout is already filed by the build.

checks.what: Report-mode exit codes of the app at HEAD
checks.evidence: missing value: exit 2 (1,991 ms); unwritable path: exit 3 (121 ms), no file; plain run: exit 0, schema 1, core.foldersVanished 0, unreadable 0, OutcomeNotes visible False

checks.what: Throw mode (exit 70)
checks.command: HookCases.ps1 throw mode with the FsaWindowHook startup hook
checks.evidence: artifacts/window-hook is not built in this tree, and the hook's arming was not set up. The slice's diff does not touch App.xaml.cs's exit path, and O-013 left exit 70 to the existing cases.

checks.what: The slice's window script, Cases A and B, on this PC
checks.evidence: It puts the app's window on the person's desktop. The Sandbox report-mode run of the same app on a live C:\ replaced it.

checks.what: Pre-slice app on a live C:\ for comparison
checks.evidence: Not repeated in this validation. Q-016's record says the pre-slice Sandbox whole-C:\ run had 3 unreadable rows with error 2, which matches the 3 folders Windows deleted beyond my 5.

checks.what: Delete-pending folder (open 5) and folder replaced by a file (listing 87) on a real walk
checks.evidence: The design leaves both unreadable on purpose. They are pinned only by the truth-table rows (5,false) and (87,true) in ScannerFailedKindTests, which passed in the suite.

criteria.criterion: 1. A root child queued by the root's listing and deleted before its open (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, 2) is not called unreadable
criteria.how: Sandbox, fix against pre-slice on NTFS, ReFS, SMB loopback and a mapped letter: the raw open returns 2. The pre-slice build records it (error 2 NothingListed); the fix counts it in FoldersVanished with Unreadable 0. Live Sandbox C:\ (scan program and app): 8 deleted folders, unreadable 0. The suite (VanishedFolderTests) also passes.

criteria.criterion: 2. A deeper folder whose parent was deleted too (open 3) is not called unreadable, and its top-level row counts no UnreadableBelow
criteria.how: Sandbox: y deleted after its listing makes y\w open with 3 on NTFS, ReFS, SMB and a mapped letter. The pre-slice build records it; the fix counts it in FoldersVanished with Unreadable 0. That row y's UnreadableBelow is 0 comes from VanishedFolderTests.AFolderUnderADeletedParentIsGoneAndItsRowCountsNoUnreadableBelow passing in the 1346-test suite; my scan program did not print rows.

criteria.criterion: 3. Refused and partly read folders are still recorded
criteria.how: The suite passes, including VanishedFolderTests.RefusedAndPartlyReadFoldersAreStillRecordedBesideADeletedOne (deny ACE 5 and partial listing 995). In the Sandbox, folders cut off by share removal (67), a removed mapped letter (3) and a detached ReFS volume (3) all stayed recorded NothingListed with FoldersVanished 0.

criteria.criterion: 4. Gone versus unreadable is decided from the open's outcome (truth table)
criteria.how: ScannerFailedKindTests.FolderVanishedIsTrueOnlyForARefusedOpenThatFoundNoFolderOrNoPath passes in the suite. Real codes seen in the Sandbox match it: 2 and 3 with nothing opened count as deleted, 67 does not, and 3 with the root failing stays unreadable.
The suite passes (AMissingRootIsRootUnreadableAndCountsNoVanishedFolder, RootTests). In Sandbox run 1 the scan program on an unmapped Y:\t gave RootUnreadable rootError=3 with foldersVanished=0.

criteria.criterion: 6. A deleted folder with subfolders the scan never saw is counted once
criteria.how: Sandbox on NTFS, ReFS, SMB and a mapped letter: deleting z (with z\inner\f.txt) and y (with y\w\x) gives folders=4 and FoldersVanished=2. Only z and y\w are counted; z\inner and y\w\x are not.

criteria.criterion: 7. A scan stopped after a folder vanished counts it
criteria.how: Code only: VanishedFolderTests.AStoppedScanCountsTheFoldersThatVanishedBeforeTheStop passes in the 1346-test suite (Cancelled, FoldersVanished 1, empty Unreadable). Not exercised in the Sandbox.

criteria.criterion: 8. Folder y deleted after its own listing: its file vanishes before sizing and its queued w opens with 3
criteria.how: Sandbox on 4 file systems: vanishedBeforeProbe=1 (y\g.txt), y\w raw open 3, FoldersVanished counts it, probeFailures=0, unreadable=0.

criteria.criterion: 9. Wording of the ending's note for deleted folders (1, 2 and 3, ASCII, no path)
criteria.how: CoveragePanelTextTests.TheFoldersVanishedNoteCountsFoldersDeletedWhileTheScanRan passes in the suite. The plural form was seen word for word in the live Sandbox app report: '8 folders were deleted while the scan ran, before they could be read; they are counted as empty folders.' The report has 0 non-ASCII characters and no path. The singular form is checked only by the unit test.

criteria.criterion: 10. The ending of a scan during which folders were deleted and nothing is unreadable
criteria.how: Published app at HEAD on the live Sandbox C:\, with 8 folders deleted rather than the planned 3: exit 0, core.unreadable 0, foldersVanished 8, the note in OutcomeNotes, UnreadableTab visible false, and the largest-files and kinds captions without 'missing'. The note is the 4th line in a box 76 px tall with 160.96 px of content, so it may need scrolling (already filed by the build).

criteria.criterion: 11. Report the scan: the same run plus the throw-mode, missing-value and unwritable-path runs
criteria.how: Live Sandbox report: schema 1 with core.foldersVanished present next to every existing core key, and exit 0. Missing value gave exit 2 and unwritable path gave exit 3, measured in the Sandbox. Throw mode (70) was not run by me; O-013, as accepted, left it to the existing cases, and the slice does not change App.xaml.cs's exit path.

criteria.criterion: 12. A folder whose delete is still pending (open 5) is left unreadable on purpose
criteria.how: As the design fixed it: unreadable on purpose, pinned by the (5,false) row of the FolderVanished theory, which passes in the suite. Not exercised on a real delete-pending folder.

criteria.criterion: 13. A queued folder replaced by a file (listing 87) is left as OpenedNothingListed on purpose
criteria.how: As the design fixed it: pinned by the (87,true) row of the theory, which passes in the suite. Not exercised live.
eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx at HEAD 5809f30: 1346 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Fitness: all 111 rules hold.

obligations.evidence:
Measured in Windows Sandbox (build 10.0.26100, SYSTEM) with the scan program at HEAD and the same program built from pre-slice Core 28d72d8.

Where 2 and 3 do mean a deleted folder:
- SMB loopback share \\127.0.0.1 and a drive letter mapped to it: a folder deleted on the server opens with 2, one under a deleted parent with 3. Fix: FoldersVanished 2, Unreadable 0. Pre-slice: both recorded unreadable.
- ReFS: the same codes and the same result.

Where the path above stops resolving, nothing is counted as deleted:
- Removed mapped letter: 3, but the root check keeps them unreadable.
- Detached ReFS volume: 3, kept unreadable the same way.
- Removed share: 67, not one of the gone codes.

Not settled:
- FAT32 and exFAT: the scanner refuses those roots with 87 on both builds, so the deleted-folder path never runs there. Pre-existing.
- DFS links and folder-hiding minifilters: none available here.
- A remote SMB server over a real network, and connection loss by network cut rather than share or mapping removal.

The measurable half holds; the rest stays open.

not_reached: The person's own proof runs per Q-016: W-001 on this PC's C:\, W-002 on OneDrive, W-003 network cuts. Whole-drive scans on this PC were not run; the live C:\ evidence is from a Windows Sandbox.

A remote SMB server over a real network, and a share lost through Wi-Fi off, server sleep or a Tailscale tunnel going down. Only loopback SMB in the Sandbox was tested, cut by deleting the share or the mapping.
DFS links whose target is down: DFS Namespaces is a Windows Server role and no namespace exists here.
Folder-hiding minifilters: none available to test under.

FAT32 and exFAT: the scanner refuses their roots with error 87 before and after this slice, so the deleted-folder path cannot be reached on them. This also suggests the app cannot scan exFAT or FAT USB sticks at all, which is worth a backlog item.
Delete-pending folders (open 5) and folders replaced by a file (listing 87) on a real walk: only the truth-table rows pin them, and the design leaves them unreadable.
Renamed or moved folders counted as deleted (N-056, waived): of the 8 deleted folders on the Sandbox C:\, 3 came from Windows itself, and nothing here tells a deleted one from a renamed one.
Throw-mode exit 70 was not run: the FsaWindowHook startup hook is not built in this tree.
File-system codes were measured on the Sandbox's build 10.0.26100; this PC runs 26300 (the build's SUBST and NTFS measurements were on this PC).

The app's window on this PC's desktop at its scaling (window script Cases A and B), including whether the deleted-folders note needs scrolling there. In the Sandbox, as SYSTEM, it measured 76 px against 160.96 px of content.

problems.where: Under the row of drive buttons (C:, D:, Z:)
problems.what: An empty horizontal scrollbar, with a track and arrows but no thumb, is drawn even though all three drive buttons fit. It looks like a stray control and suggests more drives are hidden off to the side. To the eye the grey 'Drives' label above is readable on white, though the engine measured 1.00:1.
